subject: Urban Planning
title: Tactical Urbanism: Testing Before Zoning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tactical Urbanism: Testing Before Zoning.

hook.text: New York tested pedestrian plazas in Times Square using lawn chairs and orange cones before making them permanent.

buildup.text: Tactical urbanism tests changes cheaply and temporarily — painted bike lanes, pop-up parks, weekend street closures.

discovery.text: If the test works, the city makes it permanent. If it fails, paint washes off and cones go back to the garage.

twist.text: Critics say tactical urbanism bypasses community input. Supporters say it replaces years of debate with evidence.

climax.text: COVID accelerated tactical urbanism. Hundreds of cities closed streets for dining and walking — many permanently.

punchline.text: Try it for a month. Measure it. Then decide. Faster than any zoning hearing.

quiz.question: What is tactical urbanism?
options: Military strategies applied to urban evacuation planning
Cheap, temporary tests of urban changes before making them permanent
Using tactical voting to influence zoning board decisions
